## Bank Account (512) — Movement History & Running Balance

The account opened on **2023-01-01 with a €45,000 opening balance** (OB-2023). The 200 transactions shown run through **2024-01-09**, where the running balance stands at **€29,943.44**.

### Key observations

**Lowest liquidity point:** The minimum running balance was **€20,030.18 on 2023-05-17** (after payment BK23-0067 of €797.64). This came at the end of a sustained drawdown through early-to-mid May, when several large outflows (e.g., €5,658.88 on May 7, €3,474.97 and €1,980 on May 15, €2,900.46 on May 16) outpaced incoming receipts.

**Overall trend:** The balance generally oscillates between roughly €20,000 and €50,000:
- **Q1 2023:** Gradual decline from €45,000 to ~€26,700 by end of April.
- **May 2023:** The trough (~€20,000 mid-month), followed by a strong recovery to ~€45,700 by May 27.
- **Mid-year:** A peak of **€49,861.49 on 2023-06-26**, then another dip to ~€23,366 by late July.
- **H2 2023:** Recovery with a high of **€52,900.22 on 2023-11-26** (the maximum in the period), before easing back.
- **Year-end / early 2024:** Balance drifted down to ~€33,200 at end of December and ~€29,943 by January 9, 2024.

**Recurring patterns visible in the data:** a €350 charge at the start of each quarter (likely a bank fee) and a recurring €1,980 monthly payment (likely rent or a similar fixed cost).

**Bottom line:** Liquidity never went negative, but the tightest moment was **mid-May 2023 (~€20,000)** — roughly a 55% drop from the opening balance — before cash inflows restored the position.

## Daily Posting Calendar — Summary

The calendar (shown here for the first 200 days, **2023-01-01 through 2023-07-19**) reveals a generally low-volume, irregular posting pattern: most days have **0–2 journal entries**, with occasional peaks of 3–4 and a single maximum of **5 entries on 2023-04-16**.

### Most striking anomaly

**The 5-day dead zone from 2023-01-19 to 2023-01-23 — zero entries for five consecutive days.** This is the longest gap in the entire period shown, and it sits within a broader pattern: January is markedly sparser than every subsequent month (roughly 18 entries total, with three multi-day gaps: Jan 19–23, Jan 26–27, and Jan 29–31), whereas by April–May, activity is nearly daily (April has only 4 zero-days).

### Structural hypothesis (explicitly a hypothesis, not an established fact)

The January sparseness — and the Jan 19–23 gap in particular — could reflect a **system or process ramp-up**: for example, the accounting system may have gone live at the start of 2023, with entries initially posted in irregular manual batches before a steadier posting routine was established from February–March onward. Alternative explanations (period-close lockout, staffing gaps, or entries posted retroactively under later dates) cannot be ruled out from this data alone; confirming would require checking system logs, entry creation timestamps vs. posting dates, or business calendars.

Secondary observation: the single-day peak of **5 entries on 2023-04-16** (a Sunday) is also unusual and could hypothetically indicate a batch or catch-up posting — again, unverified from this data.

## Revenue accumulation over time

Broadly yes — revenue accumulates at roughly **25,000–26,000 per month** on average — but there are a few clear deviations:

**Slowdowns:**
- **August 2023** is the weakest month by far: only ~14,560 added (cumulative went from ~172,438 at end of July to ~186,996 at end of August), well below the typical pace.
- **January 2024** is also soft: ~19,025 added (312,142 → 331,166).

**Accelerations:**

- **Spring 2024** also runs hot: March–May 2024 each add roughly 28,000–31,000 (e.g., May 2024 added ~31,145, from 411,859 to 443,004).

### Summary

- **Full year 2023:** ~312,142 in revenue.
- **First half of 2024:** ~157,064 more (through end of June, cumulative 469,206) — an annualized pace slightly ahead of 2023.

So the trajectory is close to linear overall, but with a visible **dip in August 2023**, a **strong Q4 2023 finish**, a **slow January 2024 start**, and a **renewed acceleration in spring 2024**. Individual postings are small and frequent (mostly a few hundred to ~4,700 each), so the swings reflect invoice volume/timing rather than any single large transaction.

## Ledger Posting Analysis

The query returned every posting line in chronological order with a running debit total. The result shown covers **200 lines from 2023-01-01 through 2023-03-28**, by which point the **cumulative debit turnover reaches 289,822.36**. (Note: the output was capped at 200 rows, so if the ledger extends beyond late March 2023, the full turnover would be higher than this figure.)

### Unusually large postings

Yes — the accumulation clearly reveals one outlier:

- **The opening balance entry on 2023-01-01 (journal OB): a single debit of 45,000.00 to account 512 (bank)**. This one posting is roughly **7x larger** than any other debit in the ledger and accounts for the cumulative total jumping immediately to 45,000 on day one.

By comparison, all other postings fall into a normal operational range:
- Typical sales invoices (SA, account 411): ~1,000–5,700
- Purchases (PU): mostly a few hundred to ~4,800
- Payroll (PY, account 641): the largest recurring items at ~6,045 (January) and ~6,375 (February)
- Bank settlements (BK): mirror the invoice amounts, up to ~5,750

### Trend

After the opening balance spike, the cumulative line grows steadily and smoothly — roughly **55,000 in January, ~91,000 in February, and ~93,000 in March-to-date** — indicating consistent monthly activity with no anomalies other than the initial capital/opening posting.

**Conclusion:** Debit turnover through the shown period is **289,822.36**, and the only unusually large single posting is the **45,000 opening balance debit**, which is expected and not suspicious in nature.

## Journal Entries Ranked by Amount

The full ranked list is shown above (200 rows returned; the list may be truncated if more entries exist). Here's the summary of what it shows:

### Distribution of amounts

- **Typical entry:** The vast majority of entries cluster tightly between roughly **€5,250 and €7,400** — routine sales invoices (SA), purchase invoices (PU), and their matching bank payments (BK).
- **Payroll (PY):** Monthly entries between **€7,845 and €9,806**, rising steadily from 2023 to 2025 — a normal, consistent pattern.
- **VAT settlements (GJ):** Quarterly entries between **€11,314 and €19,264** — recurring and proportionate to activity, nothing unusual.

### Statistical outlier

- **OB-2023 (posted 2023-01-01, journal OB) — €45,000.** This is the single clear outlier: it is **more than 2.3× the next-largest entry** (VAT-2024-Q4 at €19,264.82) and roughly **8× the typical transaction**. However, its document number, journal code, and January 1st posting date indicate it is an **opening balance entry**, which is expected to be large — so while statistically extreme, it is not inherently suspicious. It is worth noting it is a perfectly round figure (€45,000.00), which merits verification against the prior-period closing balance.

### Suspicion assessment

- No other entries stand out as anomalous. Invoice amounts are consistently matched by bank entries of identical amounts within 1–2 months (e.g., SI25-0234 for €6,796.42 followed by BK25-0477 for the same amount), which is a healthy invoice-to-payment pattern rather than a red flag.
- Payroll and VAT entries follow regular monthly/quarterly cadences with gradual growth — no spikes, duplicates, or off-cycle postings visible.

**Bottom line:** OB-2023 at €45,000 is the only statistical outlier. It appears to be a legitimate opening balance, though its round amount justifies a routine check against prior-year records. Nothing else in the data looks suspicious.
